AI agents now write trading strategies and ask for capital. AlphaCourt is a checkpoint, or gateway, between the agent and the broker. Connected over the Model Context Protocol, it holds each request for capital and puts the strategy on trial: a prosecutor, a defence and a judge argue over the output of deterministic tests, and an \emph{exhibit rule}, enforced in code, strikes any finding that cites no damaging test.
On simulated cases with known truth, a court run by the small open model Qwen3 8B stopped 46 of 46 flawed strategies and deployed 52 of 58 honest ones. % source: results/e1.json -> cells.court/small.guilty_stopped; results/e1.json -> cells.court/small.innocent_deployed
Without the rule, the same model deployed 0 of 58 honest strategies reviewing alone, and 18 of 58 when shown the test results. Evidence is not enough; the rule is what lets honest work through. % source: results/e1.json -> cells.single/small.innocent_deployed; results/e1.json -> cells.single_exhibits/small.innocent_deployed
Applying fixed pass/fail thresholds to the same tests, with no model at all, does as well. The court adds a readable trial record, but its stated reasons are often wrong, and a court run by Gemma 3 12B stopped only 26 of 46 flawed strategies. % source: results/e1.json -> cells.court/mid.guilty_stopped
Everything is simulated and no real order is placed.
